blocks.orig: Located on the southern half of the African continent, Tanzania is a truly versatile holiday destination. Whether you’re someone who prefers to spend their holiday time in a more active way or someone who just needs a good book and a spot on the beach to relax, this beautiful country has something to offer you.
blocks.html: Tanzania sits in the southern half of the African continent and is a remarkably versatile place for a holiday. Whether you like to spend your time away being active, or you simply want a good book and a quiet spot on the sand, this beautiful country has something for you.

blocks.orig: And speaking of beaches—did you know that Tanzania is home to some of the most breathtaking white sand beaches in the world? Let’s discover the best beaches of Tanzania now.
blocks.html: And since beaches came up: were you aware that some of the world’s most breathtaking stretches of white sand lie in Tanzania? Let’s explore the finest ones.

blocks.orig: Top 7 most beautiful beaches in Tanzania
blocks.html: The 7 most beautiful beaches in Tanzania

blocks.orig: Paje Beach and Jambiani Beach are, by many, considered to be Zanzibar’s most beautiful beaches. White sand, crystal blue water, a number of bars and restaurants at your disposal, and many accommodation options to choose from definitely make it hard to pass on. However, that’s not really its main selling point.
blocks.html: Many people regard Paje Beach and Jambiani Beach as Zanzibar’s finest beaches. With white sand, crystal blue water, a range of bars and restaurants on hand and plenty of places to stay, they are hard to pass up. Yet none of that is really the main attraction.

blocks.orig: Paje Beach is a real paradise for those interested in kite surfing, as every year, thousands of enthusiasts from all over the world visit this beautiful place due to favourable winds, lack of sea urchins, and shallow water. If you too enjoy kitesurfing, it would be best to plan your holiday from June to August or December to February, as that’s when you can expect the best winds. Besides, wouldn’t it be great to escape the cold and darkness winter brings to most places?
blocks.html: For anyone into kite surfing, Paje Beach is a true paradise: thanks to favourable winds, shallow water and an absence of sea urchins, thousands of enthusiasts from across the globe come here every year. If kitesurfing is your thing too, the best time to plan your holiday is June to August or December to February, when the winds are at their best. And who would not want to escape the cold, dark winter that most places have at that time of year?

blocks.orig: Our insider tip: be sure to go to at high tide to enjoy those beaches to the fullest.
blocks.html: A tip from us: visit at high tide to get the most out of these beaches.

blocks.orig: Ras Kutani Beach, located on Tanzania’s mainland, is a beautiful beach located in the proximity of Dar es Salaam—Tanzania’s biggest city. If you are looking for an ideal location for a quick gateway when the buzz of the city becomes overwhelming or when you want to fully immerse yourself in Tanzania’s beauty, this high-end lodge is the place to be.
blocks.html: On the Tanzanian mainland, not far from Dar es Salaam (the country’s largest city), you will find the beautiful Ras Kutani Beach. When the buzz of the city gets too much, or when you simply want to soak up Tanzania’s beauty, this high-end lodge is an ideal spot for a quick getaway.

blocks.orig: And for those who prefer a more active vacation, Ras Kutani Beach offers a number of activities for you to choose from, including snorkelling, during which you’ll have the opportunity to explore The Chyko’s shipwreck, bodyboarding, or trip to the tropical forest located nearby where you can admire different monkey species.
blocks.html: If you would rather keep busy on holiday, Ras Kutani Beach has a range of activities to pick from: snorkelling, which gives you the chance to explore The Chyko’s shipwreck, bodyboarding, or an outing to the tropical forest close by where you can watch various species of monkey.

blocks.orig: Located in the north of Zanzibar, Nungwi Beach is arguably one of the most popular beaches in Tanzania—and why wouldn’t it be? With white sand and crystal clear waters, it is an ideal destination for anyone who appreciates relaxing surrounded by beautiful views.
blocks.html: Nungwi Beach, at the northern tip of Zanzibar, is arguably one of Tanzania’s most popular beaches, and it is easy to see why. Its white sand and crystal clear water make it perfect for anyone who likes to unwind with beautiful views all around.

blocks.orig: The coastline is more rocky here, which means at high tide there are only a few places where you can still sit on the beach. But the views make it all worth it! From Nungwi, you can see both sunset and sunrise over the ocean.
blocks.html: The shoreline here is rockier, so at high tide only a handful of spots remain where you can still sit on the beach. The views more than make up for it, though: from Nungwi you can watch both the sunrise and the sunset over the ocean.

blocks.orig: Since there are no coral reefs close to the beach, it’s a good place for surfing and windsurfing enthusiasts. It’s also a good place to start snorkel and dolphin trips from.
blocks.html: Because there are no coral reefs right by the beach, it suits surfers and windsurfers well. It’s also a convenient starting point for snorkelling and dolphin trips.

blocks.orig: Combined with a number of restaurants serving traditional food, bars, as well as some sleeping accommodation options in surrounding areas, Nungwi Beach is definitely a destination you should consider when you’re looking for the best beaches in Tanzania.
blocks.html: Add in a selection of restaurants serving traditional dishes, bars and a number of places to sleep in the surrounding area, and Nungwi Beach is certainly one to keep in mind when you are hunting for the best beaches in Tanzania.

blocks.orig: Fanjove Island, the smallest of the islands making up the Songo Songo Archipelago, is a great destination for anyone who’s looking for a truly remote adventure. There are only six bandas on it, which means that you’ll be surrounded by (almost) nothing but nature!
blocks.html: Fanjove Island is the smallest of the islands in the Songo Songo Archipelago and a wonderful choice if you want a genuinely remote adventure. With only six bandas on the island, you will have (almost) nothing around you but nature!

blocks.orig: Fanjove Island used to be uninhibited, except for a handful of fishermen who used it as a fishing base from time to time. This allowed all the island’s flora and fauna to survive. Today, visitors can marvel at the prolific wildlife, which includes green turtles, spinner dolphins, seabirds, coconut crabs, tropical fish, and humpback whales, just to name a few. Not to mention the miles of preserved coral reefs, which are home to striking marine life.
blocks.html: For a long time nobody lived on Fanjove Island, apart from a few fishermen who occasionally used it as a base. That is why its plants and animals have survived intact. Visitors today can enjoy abundant wildlife: green turtles, spinner dolphins, seabirds, coconut crabs, tropical fish and humpback whales, to name only a few. Then there are the miles of untouched coral reef, teeming with striking sea creatures.

blocks.orig: If you’re unsure whether you want to spend your days in Tanzania exploring the wildlife or relaxing on the beach, Saadani National Park might be the ideal location for you. Being one of the few places where the bush meets the beach, this national park gives you the opportunity to spend the day observing the fauna and flora and relaxing on the beach right after.
blocks.html: Can’t decide whether to spend your days in Tanzania watching wildlife or lying on the beach? Then Saadani National Park could be just right for you. It is one of the few places where the bush meets the beach, so you can spend the day watching animals and plants and head straight to the sand afterwards to relax.

blocks.orig: The park itself is surrounded by several villages, which you might want to visit if your interest lies in history. One especially worth mentioning is the namesake of the national park—the Saadani village, which used to be a crucial harbour town, as well as East Africa’s slave trading centre.
blocks.html: Several villages surround the park, and they are worth a visit if history interests you. The one that deserves a special mention is the village the park is named after: Saadani, once an important harbour town and the centre of the slave trade in East Africa.

blocks.orig: The Vumawimbi Beach, on Pemba Island, allows you to admire the everyday life of Zanzibar fishermen as they cycle to their traditional boat and start the day filled with fishing ahead of them. Its rich and thriving coral reef, which is home to numerous marine species, makes it a great location for snorkelling lovers.
blocks.html: At Vumawimbi Beach on Pemba Island you can watch the daily routine of Zanzibar’s fishermen as they cycle down to their traditional boats and set off for a day of fishing. The rich, thriving coral reef just offshore is home to countless marine species, which makes it an excellent spot for anyone who loves snorkelling.

blocks.orig: Those who are looking to relax will be able to do so in the company of soft white sand and beautiful crystal blue water, surrounded by swaying palm trees and an ambiance that just screams peace and quiet.
blocks.html: If relaxing is what you are after, you can do so on soft white sand beside beautiful crystal blue water, with palm trees swaying overhead and an atmosphere of complete peace and quiet.

blocks.orig: Rather than pointing out an individual beach located on the island, we decided to include it as a whole, as there are too many to choose from. While Mafia Island might not be as popular among visitors as Zanzibar, it’s a dream come true, especially for those who enjoy diving.
blocks.html: Instead of singling out one beach on the island, we have included the whole island, simply because there are too many to choose between. Mafia Island may draw fewer visitors than Zanzibar, but it is a dream destination, above all for divers.

blocks.orig: If you visit from October to April, you might be able to swim with whale sharks—you might have to try a few days in a row, as sightings are not guaranteed, but it’ll be worth it in the end. After all, how many people can say that they swam with whale sharks? You can also snorkel in the Marine Park, where you’ll have the chance to see incredible coral reefs, as well as marine wildlife, like dolphins, turtles, and octopuses.
blocks.html: Come between October and April and you may get to swim alongside whale sharks. Sightings are never guaranteed, so you might need to head out several days running, but the reward is worth the effort. How many people can claim they have swum with whale sharks, after all? The Marine Park offers snorkelling too, with incredible reefs and sea creatures such as dolphins, turtles and octopuses.

blocks.orig: And for those who prefer more “down-to-earth” activities, there are a few things to do as well—for example, you can visit the nearby Chole Island, where you will feel like time has stopped, or the old lighthouse located on the north part of the Mafia Island.
blocks.html: If you prefer activities that are a little more “down-to-earth”, there are options too. You could visit nearby Chole Island, where time seems to have stood still, or the old lighthouse at the northern end of Mafia Island.

blocks.orig: Other Tanzania Beaches You May Want to Visit
blocks.html: More Tanzanian beaches worth a visit

blocks.orig: There are so many beautiful beaches to visit in Tanzania that we couldn’t possibly fit all of them into one article. So, here are some additional places, aside from the ones we already mentioned, that you should at least consider visiting next time you’re in Tanzania.
blocks.html: Tanzania has so many beautiful beaches that there is no way to fit them all into a single article. Below are a few more places, beyond the ones above, that deserve at least a thought the next time you are in Tanzania.

blocks.orig: Located close to Pemba Island, Misali Island is a good destination for those who are more active vacationers. Not only is the snorkelling experience amazing, but you can also choose from a plethora of nature trails to truly discover the beauty of this island.
blocks.html: Just off Pemba Island lies Misali Island, a good choice if you like to stay active on holiday. The snorkelling is amazing, and there is also a wide choice of nature trails that let you discover the island’s beauty properly.

blocks.orig: Misali Island is uninhabited due to the lack of fresh water, and tourists are not allowed to camp, so you need to find accommodation on Pemba Island. Still, despite not having any native inhabitants, it was and continues to be an important fishing site.
blocks.html: Misali Island has no fresh water and is therefore uninhabited, and camping is not permitted for tourists, so you will need to stay on Pemba Island. Even without permanent residents, the island was and still is an important fishing ground.

blocks.orig: It also served as a spiritual site due to the belief that the island’s caves are inhabited by the ancestors’ spirits. Even today, some people leave offerings at the caves’ entrances, believing that it will ensure great health and large catches.
blocks.html: It has also long been a spiritual place, because of the belief that the spirits of the ancestors live in the island’s caves. To this day some people leave offerings at the cave entrances in the hope of good health and plentiful catches.

blocks.orig: Also known as Oyster Bay, Coco Beach is a place that truly combines the best of both worlds. While you are located within Dar es Salaam, giving you quick access to anything you might need, you can also feel as if you were on a tropical island due to the beautiful scenery all around you. This is not to mention that Coco Beach offers several outdoor activities you can partake in, such as surfing, outdoor concerts and beach parties.
blocks.html: Coco Beach, also called Oyster Bay, genuinely offers the best of both worlds. You are inside Dar es Salaam, so everything you might need is close at hand, yet the beautiful surroundings make it feel as though you are on a tropical island. On top of that, Coco Beach hosts a range of outdoor activities you can join, from surfing to open-air concerts and beach parties.

blocks.orig: This is the beach where most locals use to go, which gives it a different vibe—local food vendors, music, many people strolling. You want to feel the vibe of local Tanzanian city life ? Go to Coco Beach!
blocks.html: This is the beach most locals head to, and that gives it a vibe of its own: food vendors, music and plenty of people out for a stroll. Want to feel the pulse of everyday city life in Tanzania? Then Coco Beach is the place!

blocks.orig: The final position on our list is Kunduchi Beach, located, once again, close to Dar es Salaam. This destination will be a good one if you’re travelling with children, as close by is Kunduchi Wet ‘n’ Wild—the largest water park in East Africa.
blocks.html: Rounding off our list is Kunduchi Beach, once again not far from Dar es Salaam. It is a smart pick for families with children, because Kunduchi Wet ‘n’ Wild, East Africa’s biggest water park, is right next door.

blocks.orig: It’s also a good place for history geeks who can visit the remnants of an XVI-century mosque and XVIII-century pillar tombs adorned with Chinese porcelain, as well as Mbweni graves, although those are located a little further away.
blocks.html: History lovers are well served too: nearby you can see the remains of an XVI-century mosque and XVIII-century pillar tombs decorated with Chinese porcelain, and, a little further away, the Mbweni graves.

blocks.orig: Next to Kundichi Beach, we would like to mention Mbudya Island (close to Kunduchi) and Bongoyo Island (close to Masaki) which are both amazing beaches. A local boat takes you there. These are uninhabited islands where locals go in the weekend. On Mbudya you can even find giant coconut crabs.
blocks.html: Alongside Kundichi Beach we also want to mention Mbudya Island (near Kunduchi) and Bongoyo Island (near Masaki), both blessed with wonderful stretches of sand. A local boat ferries you across. Nobody lives on either island, and residents of the city head there at the weekend. On Mbudya you may even come across giant coconut crabs.

blocks.orig: Tanzania is a diverse country that offers you not only stunning views, beautiful beaches, and impressive mountains but also hard-to-forget cultural experiences. The land is full of history, waiting for anyone willing to uncover it. If you’re lucky enough, you might also experience wildlife encounters that will be stuck in your mind for a very long time.
blocks.html: Tanzania is a varied country, offering not just stunning scenery, beautiful beaches and impressive mountains, but also cultural experiences that stay with you. The land is steeped in history, ready for anyone willing to explore it. With a bit of luck you may also have wildlife encounters you will remember for years to come.

blocks.orig: Still, it’s no secret that one of the reasons why people choose to visit this country is because of its beaches. Tanzania beaches are some of the most beautiful coastlines in the world, and the ones on our list certainly prove that.
blocks.html: Even so, it is no secret that the beaches are one of the main reasons people decide to visit. The coastline of Tanzania ranks among the most beautiful in the world, and the beaches on our list show exactly why.
